subject: Post-call: embed+stream fit, function-call constraints & licensing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Turner <eliza.turner@heliox.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: embed+stream fit, function-call constraints & licensing next steps

Hi Eliza / Nick — great to meet today. Thanks for walking through HelioX's retrieval pipeline and the production constraints. Quick recap from our side plus suggested next steps so we all have alignment.

Summary of pain points you emphasized:
- Latency at 99p under high QPS (customer-facing search with 500–1k qps peak) — current infra sometimes spikes >250ms.
- Cost sensitivity for reranking layer (hundreds of millions of documents indexed; need per-query price clarity).
- Need for streaming responses into the UI and deterministic structured outputs for downstream ingestion (function-calling / JSON schema).
- Security: SOC 2 attestation, SSO (SAML), and EU data residency for a subset of telemetry.

What we believe is the right fit (technical):
- Redwood hosted with a Dedicated pool for your high-QPS rerank flows (predictable throughput, autoscale headroom).
- Use embeddings for coarse retrieval + Redwood rerank (embed -> vector search -> rerank streaming responses).
- Streaming + function-calling to emit a compact JSON payload (slots: title, snippet, action_hint) — reduces client-side parsing and preserves structured logs.
- KV prefix caching and request-aware batching to hit your latency targets without blowing up token costs.

Open constraints we need from you (to finalize pilot scope):
1) Typical query length and 95/99 latency SLO targets per endpoint.
2) Expected QPS per minute and burst profile (sliding window).
3) Redaction/data residency rules (which fields must never leave EU).
4) Procurement / licensing timeline (preferred PO cadence and billing owner).

Proposed immediate next steps (week of Jun 21):
- Redwood: share a draft technical scope and a starter pricing sheet (attached). Marissa to send by EOD 6/20.
- HelioX: share a sample of anonymized queries and a short trace of 1 hour peak load (we only need request rates & length distributions). Nick to confirm by 6/23.
- Technical sync (eng): 60-minute session with your infra and our runtime team to walk the integration pattern (we suggested 6/24 or 6/25).

Attachments I will include: proposed technical scope, price schedule, and an MVP integration checklist.

If that looks right, we can convert the scope into a pilot SOW and lock in reserved capacity for the rerank path.

Thanks again — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Eliza Turner <eliza.turner@heliox.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Nick Ramos <nick.ramos@heliox.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: embed+stream fit, function-call constraints & licensing next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is a helpful summary. Quick answers inline and two clarifications from our side: 

Inline: 
- Latency: our immediate target is p95 < 120ms, p99 < 200ms for the first token of the rerank result. End-to-end currently sits at ~260ms p99 during peaks.
- QPS: steady-state 300 qps, with bursts to ~900 qps for 10–20 minute windows during promotions.
- Data residency: search telemetry for EU customers must remain in EU region; the content corpus is global.
- Security: SOC 2 is required; SSO via SAML mandatory; we may require a custom contract clause around telemetry retention.

Clarifications: 
1) Can Redwood's streaming path emit both the streaming text and a final function-call JSON so the client can immediately show partial text and then commit structured metadata? We want the UX to be responsive but also need the final JSON for downstream systems.
2) Pricing: we need a clear per-rerank request cost and an estimate of monthly spend at 500K queries. Can you also call out any overage terms for burst capacity?

We will prepare a small, anonymized query trace and share by 6/23. Also happy to run the eng sync on 6/24 — prefer 10:00–11:00 PT.

Best,
Eliza
CTO, HelioX Solutions
eliza.turner@heliox.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: embed+stream fit, function-call constraints & licensing next steps

Eliza — thanks for the quick clarifications. A couple things from commercial side to make procurement smoother: 
- We can provide an anchor per-request price for the rerank pipeline (embed + rerank) and an optional reserved-capacity discount if you commit monthly throughput. I'll attach a sample tiered schedule in the follow-up.
- For bursts we offer two options: (1) short-term burst credits billed at a higher per-request rate, or (2) pre-purchased burst blocks that smooth monthly spend. We’ll outline both in the pricing sheet.

Immediate asks from HelioX for next week: 
1) Confirm procurement contact and PO timing — we typically need 2–3 weeks to turn a standard SOW.
2) Agree on a pilot success metric (for the pilot SOW): suggested metric p99 < 180ms under 300 qps sustained and accuracy delta <= 2% vs current reranker.

I’ll be on the 6/24 technical sync as well.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: embed+stream fit, function-call constraints & licensing next steps

Thanks all — consolidated next steps and deliverables below. Attaching the same files formally for your procurement and eng teams.

Deliverables we will send by EOD 6/20 (attached):
- Technical scope (heliox-technical-scope-v1.pdf): outlines the integration pattern (embed -> search -> rerank streaming + function-call), region/residency options, and KV caching assumptions.
- Pricing schedule (redwood-embedstream-price-schedule.xlsx): per-request costs, reserved capacity tiers, and burst-block options.
- MVP integration checklist (mvp-integration-checklist.docx): list of API hooks, sample schema for function outputs, and required telemetry fields.

Action items (owners):
- HelioX: share anonymized query trace + peak trace by 6/23 (Nick).
- Redwood eng: run technical sync 6/24 10:00–11:00 PT (Karthik, Marissa).
- Rediscover: define pilot SLOs in draft SOW (Marissa + Ben) — target to deliver draft SOW by 6/25.

On the streaming + function-call question: yes — the runtime can emit partial text chunks to the client while buffering a deterministic function-call JSON that is emitted as a final event (we’ll demo this in the tech sync). This pattern matches reducing perceived latency while guaranteeing structured outputs for downstream ingest.

If that aligns, we’ll lock the 6/24 slot and I’ll send calendar invites shortly.

Thanks — Marissa

--
